claims.sentence: A scan by GPTZero found 100 fabricated references, most of them to works that do not exist, in 53 papers accepted at NeurIPS 2025 \citep{ansari2026compound}, and a scan of the 2025 papers accepted at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS and USENIX Security estimated that 0.38--0.81\% of their references were likely hallucinated \citep{russinovich2026phantom}.
claims.claim: A GPTZero scan found 100 fabricated references, most to non-existent works, in 53 papers accepted at NeurIPS 2025.
claims.excerpt:
Despite review by 3–5 expert researchers per paper, these fabricated citations evaded detection, appearing in 53 published papers (≈1% of all accepted papers). We develop a five-category taxonomy
that classifies hallucinations by their failure mode: Total Fabrication (66%)
claims.location: Abstract, p. 1; GPTZero scan described in Sec. 2.1 (Data Source), p. 3; category shares in Table 1, Sec. 3.1
claims.note: Supported. Context: the source re-analyses GPTZero's public report (secondary for the scan itself, which the sentence now attributes to GPTZero); GPTZero scanned 4,841 of the 5,290 accepted papers and human-verified each flag as a 'probable hallucination'; 'most ... do not exist' rests on 66% Total Fabrication (zero overlap with any real work); a footnote notes GPTZero's page also gives 51 papers in one place.
